paper_title: Dual effects of nitrogen and phosphorus enrichment on grassland ecosystem functioning (misaligned PCoA ordination scores relative to SampleID)
paper_authors: Journal of Ecology 113:2447-2459 (2025); DOI 10.1111/1365-2745.70105. Author-confirmed misaligned-records correction (Dryad doi:10.5061/dryad.n8pk0p37d, original v4 vs corrected v6 NP_Data_New.xlsx).

orig_v4.note: Original Dryad deposit v4 (2025-07-02). Sheet1: 60 sample rows (KO17*) x 113 columns. PCoA ordination columns (AB_PCo1 at col AI, AB_PCo2 at col AJ, etc.) were pasted misaligned relative to SampleID (col A) when merging source sheets.

corrected_v6.note: Author-supplied corrected deposit v6 (2026-05-08). Same 60x113 layout; PCoA columns re-aligned to their correct SampleID. SampleID (col A) and richness columns (Plant_Rich col P, AB_Rich col Q) unchanged between versions.

claims.claim_atom: In the original Dryad deposit (NP_Data.xlsx, Sheet1) the AB_PCo1 ordination score for SampleID KO17A3 (row 7, AB_Rich=1.791759=ln(6) species) is AI7=0.144522648551141. This exact value is also carried by rows 2, 5 and 10 (SampleIDs KO17A1/KO17A22/KO17A20), all of which are AB_Rich=1.609438=ln(5) samples. A PCoA ordinates each sample by its full community composition, so two samples with different species richness cannot legitimately land on an identical axis-1 coordinate to 15 significant figures. The author-supplied correction (Dryad v6, NP_Data_New.xlsx) re-aligns the PCoA columns to SampleID and this same cell becomes AI7=-0.761154394232619, confirming that the original value did not belong to KO17A3 — the ordination columns had been pasted out of register with SampleID when source sheets were merged. The author explicitly states this misalignment does not change the published results. This is a misaligned_records / provenance_mismatch: the number physically present at a locus is genuine ordination output but is attached to the wrong sample. It is invisible to file-internal numeric detectors: (1) duplicate-column detector compares whole columns for byte-identity or constant offset — the AB_PCo1 column as a whole is not a duplicate of any other column; (2) fixed-offset / paired-ratio detectors look for column-to-column arithmetic relations — none exists here, the corruption is a within-column row permutation; (3) the original AB_PCo1 series and the corrected AB_PCo1 series are neither equal, offset, nor linearly related (the rows are permuted), so a src-vs-tgt relationship verifier returns 'independent'. Detection requires knowing that PCoA scores must be a deterministic function of the per-sample community composition — external ecological/statistical reasoning plus the correction notice, not a numeric pattern in the file.
claims._adjudication: inconsistent: 原始 deposit の AB_PCo1 列は SampleID に対して行ずれ(misaligned)して貼り付けられており、KO17A3(AB_Rich=ln6)の AI7=0.144523 は AB_Rich=ln5 の複数サンプル(row2/5/10)と 15 桁完全一致する。PCoA スコアは各サンプルの群集組成の決定論的関数なので、異なる種数の行が同一座標を持つことは統計的に不可能。著者修正版(Dryad v6)では同セルが -0.761154 に変わり、元の値がこのサンプルに属さないこと(列のずれ)を裏付ける。B3 検出器は列間の数値関係(重複/定数オフセット/線形)を探すが、これは列内の行順列であり src-vs-tgt は independent と判定される→ no_flag。発見には PCoA が組成の関数であるという外部知識+修正通知が必要。

claims.claim_atom: The SampleID column was not part of the misaligned PCoA block. Cell A2='KO17A1' in the original deposit and A2='KO17A1' in the corrected deposit are identical; the SampleID column is byte-identical across all 60 sample rows between the two versions. The sample identifiers are the stable spine against which the correction re-aligned the ordination columns, so their agreement across versions is exactly what one expects of an unaffected identity column.
claims._adjudication: consistent(clean): SampleID 列は PCoA のずれの影響を受けず、原始・修正両版で 60/60 行完全一致。KO17A1 は両版で同一。修正が列を再整列させる際の基準(spine)であり、一致は当然。clean claim としてファイル間の安定同一列を確認。

claims.claim_atom: The plant species-richness column (Plant_Rich, col P) was likewise not part of the misaligned PCoA block. Plant_Rich for SampleID KO17A1 is P2=2.70805020110221 (=ln(15) plant species) in both the original and corrected deposits, and the Plant_Rich column is identical across all 60 rows between versions. Only the ordination-score columns (Plant_PCo*, AB_PCo*, OC_PCo*, ...) were pasted out of register; the raw richness measures that feed the ordination were untouched, so this value's agreement across versions is consistent.
claims._adjudication: consistent(clean): Plant_Rich 列も PCoA ずれの影響外で、原始・修正両版で 60/60 一致。KO17A1 の ln(15)=2.708 は両版同一。序列化(ordination)に入力される生の豊富度測度は改変されていない。clean claim。

metadata._correction_doi: Dryad doi:10.5061/dryad.n8pk0p37d (original v4 2025-07-02 vs corrected v6 2026-05-08, NP_Data_New.xlsx)
metadata._correction_text: Author confirmed on PubPeer: when merging multiple source sheets, the PCoA-related columns (Plant_PCo1/2, AB_PCo1/2, OC_PCo1/2, ...) were pasted misaligned relative to SampleID; a corrected NP_Data_New.xlsx was provided. The author states the error does not affect the published results and conclusions (J. Ecology 113:2447-2459).
metadata._lane: Detector-disjoint holdout case (misaligned_records / #4). Anomaly = within-column row permutation of PCoA ordination scores relative to SampleID; the physically-present values are genuine ordination output attached to the wrong samples. Out-of-family: not a duplicate column, not a constant offset, not a paired ratio, not a cross-sheet value copy. External correction notice + the statistical fact that PCoA scores are a deterministic function of per-sample composition are required to detect it.
metadata._grounding_summary: openpyxl-parsed both Dryad deposits locally. Original AB_PCo1 (col AI) has AI2=AI5=AI7=AI10=0.144522648551141 despite rows 2/5/10 being AB_Rich=ln(5) and row 7 being AB_Rich=ln(6) — different species richness sharing an identical 15-sig-fig PCoA coordinate. Corrected v6 re-differentiates them (AI7 -> -0.761154394232619). SampleID (col A) 60/60 identical across versions; Plant_Rich (col P) 60/60 identical; AB_Rich (col Q) 59/60 identical. Confirms only the ordination-score block was permuted relative to the identity/richness spine.
metadata._detector_note: misaligned_records is outside the B3 detector family (duplicate-column / fixed-offset / paired-ratio / cross-sheet-reuse). The corruption is a row permutation WITHIN the AB_PCo1 column, not a relation BETWEEN two columns. Feeding the original AB_PCo1 series vs the corrected AB_PCo1 series to l1_relationship_verifier yields 'independent' (permuted rows are neither equal, offset, nor linearly related). The single-cell claim loci (AI7:AI7 etc.) also fall under the len<2 guard. Expected B3: no_flag on all claims.
